note: EXAMPLE ONLY, published to show the format. A real private run config, and the plugins that define its held-out domains and genres, must NOT be published or committed to a public repository before the evaluation: anyone who sees them can tune a model to the held-out sets. Keep them private and draw a fresh random nonce for every config (python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(16))"). Give every plugin with the SHA-256 of its bytes, as {"path": "plugins/tides.py", "sha256": "<sha256sum plugins/tides.py>"}: the config names a plugin by its path, so only the SHA-256 makes the commitment cover what the held-out domain or genre is, and evalgen refuses to run a plugin whose bytes differ from it. What the evaluator publishes: before the evaluation, only the two commitments that cli.py generate records in the run's manifest (seed_commitment and private_config_commitment), never the manifest itself, which holds the seed; after the evaluation, this config, its plugin files and the seed with its nonce. Anyone can then check the config with python cli.py verify-config RUN_DIR CONFIG, and regenerating the run checks every plugin against its SHA-256. Plugin paths are relative to this file. This example holds out the test-only toy domain and toy genre of tests/, which are public and hide nothing from anyone, so it names them by path alone (a checkout may change their line endings, and so their bytes): use it to demo the held-out metrics offline, e.g. python cli.py demo --mix random --private-config configs/private.example.json
